sourceInformation.genre: Stealth investigation / crime drama with a corner-management shift and a versus mode
sourceInformation.perspective: Isometric 2.5D (pixel-art 3D skeleton rigs on a tile world); HTML case-file screens
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.1 full engine (canvas 2D lighting); AI Hub session client 1.4.0; vanilla JavaScript; Web Audio
sourceInformation.artDirection: Engine-native retro-modern pixel art pushed toward grit: sodium streetlight, rain, brick rowhouses, boarded vacants
sourceInformation.animation: Engine-native procedural Humanoid rigs (poses, crouch, sprint, down), tweens and coroutine-free state machines
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written chip-synth music (layered engine tracks), synthesized effects, Web Audio formant gibberish voices with a telephone filter
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1 shared-world, 1-4 players (verified in the harness); local split-screen versus for 2 humans on one keyboard or two gamepads; no other network
sourceInformation.testing: Playwright (Chromium and WebKit) smoke runs, a scripted chase, a fake DualSense, touch-only emulation, all missions under the attract bot, two-player split-screen runs (keyboard, and two fake gamepads), and the AI Hub harness (2 players, 4 players with latency and loss, host-leave, server), all passing on the final build. Not tested: real iOS Safari, a real controller, a real TV, visual review of every scene.
sourceInformation.research: my-3D2dge handoff docs (API.md, AI_GUIDE.md), the AI Hub client source and README, and the supplied PLAN.md; knowledge of the series from memory; no web research
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown

testingFeedback: About 8 issues: the title menu stayed open over missions and attract, tail state leaked between missions, a tail could succeed with no contact, a fake pad was injected too late, toasts overlapped, my first Person constructor was broken, and two hub-harness failures (the briefing screen blocked network sends, and the no-player server copy sent nothing).
None are known to remain. The most serious were the menu over missions and the briefing blocking hub traffic; both would have broken play.
The AI Hub harness, because it found two real multiplayer bugs; running every mission under the attract bot was second.
Node syntax checks: they passed while the game was still wrong at runtime.
engineFeedback: Everything is drawn by code and still looks good: shaded rigs, canvas lighting, rain, and the ready-made pause/settings screens.
Yes. I guessed at the mouse-ground return shape and at how settings groups appear; a browser run settled both.
The investigation screens (board, cipher, wire room, box, affidavit) as a small DOM kit, the perception 'made' loop and the hub netcode.
Working out which of a very large API surface to trust without seeing it; the index helped but the card is long.
Nothing needs removing. I would merge Dialog and Shell so a canvas-plus-DOM game has one text path.
A built-in right-stick aim helper that applies the player's axis inversion.
promptFeedback: The plan's concrete data, the controller-first rules and the explicit deliverables list.
The plan describes more than a medium-effort build covers (a 72x56 map); I built to TASK.md and a smaller 48x34 map instead.
Keeping the demo complete while honoring the 10-foot rules without a real pad or TV.
A run with a real DualSense in a browser.

aiHub.name: WIRETAP
aiHub.description: Work both sides of a West Baltimore corner: photograph the crew, decode pagers, work the wire room and face the judge, then run the corner as Tee. Includes a 1-4 player shared-world versus mode.
aiHub.controls: Stick/WASD move · L2/RMB watch · R2/LMB photo · ✕/E interact · △/Q call out · Create/Tab notebook
